# Scientific review

**Correctness — PASS.** The proof establishes that the two permutations induced by multiplication force equality of the principal ideals generated by each element and its image. Hence every principal ideal is generated by its square and the finite commutative ring is reduced. A finite reduced commutative ring is a product of finite fields. Preservation of principal ideals then forces the proposed permutation to stabilize singleton-coordinate support strata. The product-of-nonzero-field-elements obstruction eliminates all odd-field factors, and a direct additive collision eliminates factors of order two. Every remaining product admits a coordinatewise scalar witness, because Frobenius squaring is bijective. Each implication and boundary condition is explicit in the proof; exhaustive small-ring tests support, but do not establish, the infinite statement.

**Originality — PASS (self-review).** The closest known source is Araújo et al., *Complete Mappings of Semigroups*, arXiv:2608.25092v1, Theorems 2.1 and 3.3 and Problem 15.12. Its theorem about one multiplicative operation supplies general structural ingredients; Problem 15.12 explicitly poses simultaneous operations, including finite rings with addition and multiplication. It does not provide the complete finite-commutative-ring existence criterion or the explicit binary-field-only characterization. A classical complete-permutation-polynomial reference (Zieve, arXiv:1312.1325) concerns a permutation and its additive translate, not both additive and multiplicative conditions in the abstract examined. Targeted external literature and mathematical-index searches did not identify an equivalent or stronger covering theorem. Search incompleteness and potential unindexed earlier formulations remain a residual risk.

**Value — PASS.** A concrete subclass of an expressly formulated 2026 simultaneous-operation open problem receives a complete if-and-only-if solution. The answer distinguishes the two independent obstructions—odd unit-group factors versus two-element additive collisions—and supplies constructions for arbitrarily many binary field factors. The product \(\mathbb F_2\times\mathbb F_4\) shows the distinction is real: each operation separately has a complete mapping, but no common permutation works. This provides a natural structural finite-ring criterion, not a restatement of a single-operation complete-mapping theorem.

**Limits and risk.** No independent audit has been performed. Bibliographic originality is limited to accessible sources and targeted searches; the theorem does not enumerate all maps or address noncommutative rings.

Self-review: passed. Independent audit: not yet performed.
